title: Limited strong nonresonance of small even Gaussian periodic potentials through second-order spectral transversality
difficulty_reason: The first-order Dirichlet transversality does not control paired even combinations of the periodic spectrum. The author controls their second spectral derivatives by the frequency-uniform rational main term 1/(4n²−j²), then constructs a detecting direction in a bounded finite set despite cancellations. Large-frequency induction and a nonzero integer numerator with bounded degree give a quantitative noncancellation bound in terms of the smallest frequency; this is transferred to a small-potential second-order bound. The square-root sublevel estimate and Gaussian union are subsequent named or standard inputs, not the new difficulty. This mechanism is independent of both the old energy-space normal form and the first-order genericity unit.

problems.difficulty_reason: The proof controls a hypergeometric transformation uniformly across five summation regimes, including indices near and beyond the moving negative parameter. Connecting adjacent chambers then proves that one matrix is invariant under every local generator, beyond checking invariance in a single diagonal basis.
